text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Foreign supermarket chains' interests are advanced by some corrupt and influential political circles which benefit materially from their support, the right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland leader Jan Olszewski said.
- The Gdansk-based Stocznia Polnocna shipyard has passed the recently finished "Sea Rover" container ship to the German contractor.
- A two day conference on cooperation between the Szczecin based universities and companies operating in the Polish- German border area started in Szczecin yesterday.
- Poland's coal mining sector received 4.6 billion zlotys of taxpayer's money in subsidies in the last five and a half years, finance ministry official Zbigniew Boniuszko said.
- Swedish Bonnier Grup will start publishing a new Polish business daily "Puls Biznesu" in January 1997. The newspaper will concentrate on the country's microeconomic issues.
- Nafta Polska petroleum holding has given up its plans to integrate fiancially the CPN petrol distribution network with the holding.
NOWA EUROPA
- National Investment Fund (NFI)-7 has appointed an advisory board which will assist the Fund's privatisation and shares' listing.
- The EU may ban Polish horses exports to Italy as the animals are transported in inhumane conditions, an EU specialist bulletin said.
- The state-owned Polish Airlines LOT will contract eight Boeing 737-800 planes late this year or early in 1997, LOT president Jan Litwinski said.
- A European Commission envoy will visit Poland in a bid to settle differences over Poland's trade policies ahead of its talks on the European Union membreship, the EU ambassador to Poland said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- If the NFI funds don't consolidate the controlled minority stakes their stock listing will be delayed, Warsaw Stock Exchange president Wieslaw Rozlucki said.

- Europol Gaz gas transit system company has obtained a 56 million zlotys credit to finance the purchase of land under the Yamal - Western Europe gas pipeline. The credit was granted by a banking consortium formed by Bank Gdanski, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy, and Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych banks.

- Poland's poultry livestock prices have declined since summer and range between 3.38 and 3.48 zlotys per kg but are still well above European average prices, the major Drosed poultry processor representatives said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY

- Almost 50 percent of Poles favour the present government petrol pricing policy, even at the cost of the foreseeable breaks in fuels distribution while 28 percent favour freeing prices, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
- The Krakow-based BPH bank has introduced a new educational credit offer at a 23.5 percent annual interest rate. The offer is addresed to undergraduate and postgraduate students.
PARKIET

- Over 54 percent of the total share trading turnover in September was made by the following brokerage firms: Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (COK BH), CBM Pekao SA, Citibrokerage, DM BIG, Creditanstalt and BRE Brokers.
- Paged foreign trade company stock is listed on the Warsaw bourse main market today. The company will introduce 910 thousand B-series shares and two million C-series shares.

- The control stake in Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) bank will be sold by the end of April 1997 and Bank Handlowy (BH) bank will follow suit, the finance ministry banking system department director Wieslaw Fedorowicz said.
